paragraphs: Policy search can improve an agent through gradient updates or through evolutionary exploration of candidate policies. The paper describes complementary strengths: deep reinforcement learning uses experience efficiently but can be unstable, while evolution strategies offer stability but need more samples. Combining them is attractive, yet synchronized updates can limit how effectively evolutionary search uses parallel computation.

AES-RL combines evolution strategies and policy gradient learning through an asynchronous framework. Its update methods are designed to support exploration and efficient use of parallel workers while retaining the useful properties of both learning approaches. The contribution therefore concerns both how the two methods interact and how their updates are scheduled.

On continuous control benchmarks, the authors report better performance and time efficiency than previous methods. These results support asynchronous integration as a practical way to make hybrid policy search more effective. The evidence concerns the evaluated benchmarks; the stated outcome is an empirical improvement in learning and runtime, rather than a universal guarantee that combining the methods always delivers all their strengths.
neurips-2020-an-efficient-asynchronous-m.tldr: AES-RL asynchronously combines evolutionary search and policy gradients, improving performance and time efficiency on continuous control benchmarks.

paragraphs: A classifier may encounter categories during testing that were absent from its labeled training examples. The paper studies this setting as learning with augmented classes. Earlier approaches used geometric patterns to discover these categories, with encouraging empirical results, but the authors identify a gap in theoretical understanding of how well such methods generalize.

Their approach uses unlabeled training data to approximate the distribution that the additional classes might follow. Under assumptions described as mild, this information makes it possible to construct an unbiased estimator of risk on the testing distribution. Here, unbiasedness concerns estimating the testing risk correctly on average; it does not mean that the resulting classifier makes no mistakes.

This estimator provides a foundation for a learning method with theoretical guarantees. The approach also accommodates environments where new classes emerge while the relative frequencies of known classes change. Experiments support its effectiveness. The central contribution is connecting information in unlabeled data to a principled training objective that accounts for a broader testing population.
neurips-2020-an-unbiased-risk-estimator-.tldr: Under mild assumptions, unlabeled data enables unbiased estimation of testing risk when previously unseen classes may appear.

paragraphs: Neural architecture design often concentrates on the operations inside a network block or the connections within it. AutoBSS examines another design choice: how those blocks are stacked to form a network. The paper argues that this configuration can materially affect performance and deserves systematic search alongside the design of individual blocks.

The method uses Bayesian optimization to search for a block stacking style. It represents candidate configurations through a code, then repeatedly refines and clusters these codes during search. The authors describe this process as finding an optimal stacking configuration in a small number of trials without biased evaluation. Its purpose is to make this architectural choice practical to optimize automatically.

On ImageNet, the searched configurations achieve 79.29% for ResNet50, 74.5% for MobileNetV2, and 77.79% for EfficientNet-B0, improving on the original baselines. Experiments also cover model compression, object detection, and instance segmentation. Together, these findings support the value of block stacking choices across the tested applications and the usefulness of AutoBSS beyond the initial classification setting.
neurips-2020-autobss-an-efficient-algori.tldr: AutoBSS uses Bayesian optimization to search block stacking configurations, improving several networks and showing benefits across multiple tasks.

paragraphs: In k-medoids clustering, each cluster is represented by an actual data point. This supports interpretable representatives and arbitrary distance measures, making the approach useful for structured objects. Its computational burden is a major obstacle: standard Partitioning Around Medoids, or PAM, requires work quadratic in the number of data points at each iteration.

BanditPAM uses a randomized approach inspired by multi-armed bandits to reduce this cost. Under data assumptions that the authors say often hold in practice, it lowers per-iteration complexity from O(n²) to O(n log n) while producing the same result with high probability. Both the assumptions and the probability qualification matter: the claim is not unconditional equivalence on every run.

Experiments on programming submissions, single-cell RNA sequencing data, and handwritten digits support the approach. The authors observe matching results with up to fourfold faster execution and up to 200-fold fewer distance calculations. These are reported experimental maxima. The findings show how reducing distance computations can make representative-based clustering practical on larger datasets while preserving the clustering quality of the compared PAM-like methods.
neurips-2020-banditpam-almost-linear-tim.tldr: BanditPAM reduces PAM’s per-iteration complexity to O(n log n), preserving its results with high probability under stated data assumptions.

paragraphs: Learning in a multilayer network requires determining how connections inside the network contributed to an output error. Backpropagation handles this effectively in artificial networks, but the paper describes it as biologically implausible. Some alternatives learn separate feedback connections, which introduces another learning problem and makes error assignment depend on how successfully those connections learn to invert forward processing.

The proposed approach obtains inversion through network dynamics. Viewed as a feedback control process, it reuses the forward transformation and lets it interact over time with fixed or random feedback. Error signals propagate through this interaction. The authors state that the dynamics guarantee accurate inversion within their scheme, removing the need to train a separate feedback system to approximate it.

They map these dynamics onto generic feedforward networks and report good performance on several supervised and unsupervised datasets. They also discuss possible connections to second-order optimization. The contribution is an alternative mechanism for credit assignment that gives temporal dynamics and feedback control a central role; it does not establish that biological brains implement this particular algorithm.
neurips-2020-biological-credit-assignmen.tldr: Dynamic inversion uses feedback control to propagate learning errors without training a separate set of inverse feedback connections.

paragraphs: Zero-shot semantic segmentation assigns category labels to pixels even when some categories have no training examples. One approach generates visual features from word embeddings and uses them to train classifiers for unseen categories. The paper identifies a weakness: a generator trained only on seen categories has no direct constraint guiding what it produces for unseen ones.

CSRL adds guidance through relationships among categories. The authors observe that category relationships are often similar in word embedding space and visual feature space. They use both pair-wise and list-wise structures to encourage generated visual features to preserve their corresponding semantic relationships. This transfers information about how seen and unseen categories relate, indirectly constraining the unseen features.

Experiments on Pascal-VOC and Pascal-Context report substantial improvements over existing methods, with gains described as approximately 7–12% and 2–5%, respectively. These findings support using category structure to improve feature generation for unseen classes. The mechanism relies on the stated observation of similarity between semantic and visual relations, rather than access to labeled visual examples of those unseen categories.
neurips-2020-consistent-structural-relat.tldr: CSRL improves zero-shot segmentation by making generated visual features preserve semantic relationships between seen and unseen categories.

paragraphs: Complex drawings contain individual strokes whose relationships determine the larger structure. CoSE approaches drawing generation by treating a drawing as a collection of composable strokes. This shifts attention toward how strokes fit together in structures such as flowcharts, extending beyond the basic objects and handwriting emphasized by earlier sequence-based approaches.

Its central component is an autoencoder that converts strokes of different lengths into representations with a fixed number of dimensions. A relational model then works with these representations to capture dependencies among strokes and predict subsequent ones. This gives the model a common representation for individual strokes while allowing it to reason about their role in the surrounding drawing.

The authors present qualitative and quantitative evidence that CoSE captures both the appearance of individual strokes and the composition of larger diagrams. They also identify interactive diagram completion as a suitable application. The important result is the combination of local stroke modeling with broader structural modeling: generating a plausible mark is only part of the task when that mark must contribute to a coherent diagram.
neurips-2020-cose-compositional-stroke-e.tldr: CoSE encodes variable-length strokes into fixed-size representations so a relational model can generate strokes within complex diagram structures.

paragraphs: A video can contain several visible objects while its soundtrack mixes sounds from only some of them. The task is to locate the objects that are actually producing sound and distinguish their categories. This is especially difficult in mixed sound scenes, where a single audio track must be related to several possible visual sources.

The paper proposes a two-stage framework. First, it aggregates candidate localization results from scenes with a single sound source to learn robust object representations. It then uses that object knowledge to produce category-aware localization maps in mixed scenes. Matching the category distributions inferred from audio and visual objects helps select which visible objects are sounding.

Agreement between the audio and visual information supplies the self-supervised learning signal. Experiments on both realistic and synthesized mixed sound videos report better filtering of silent objects and better localization of sounding objects from different classes. The approach matters because it combines learned object knowledge with cross-modal agreement, addressing both where a possible source is located and whether it is supported by the audio.
neurips-2020-discriminative-sounding-obj.tldr: A two-stage audiovisual model learns object knowledge from single-source scenes and uses category agreement to locate sounding objects in mixed scenes.

paragraphs: A discrete latent space lets a generative model represent multiple possible explanations or outcomes for an input. Complex data may require many latent classes, but that size can make downstream computation difficult. The paper highlights motion planning as an example where reasoning over a large latent representation of the environment could become intractable.

The proposed method reduces the discrete latent space of an already trained conditional variational autoencoder. Using evidential theory, it identifies which latent classes receive direct support from the particular input condition and filters out classes that lack that support. The reduction is therefore conditional on the input and is applied after training.

A central requirement is preserving multimodality: reducing the candidate space should retain the distinct possibilities the model has learned. Experiments involving image generation and human behavior prediction show that the technique can shrink the latent sample space while maintaining this diversity. The contribution is a way to simplify downstream use of a trained model without treating compression as a reason to collapse its predictions into a single outcome.
neurips-2020-evidential-sparsification-o.tldr: An evidence-based post-training filter reduces a conditional autoencoder’s discrete latent space while empirically preserving its multiple learned possibilities.

paragraphs: Photometric stereo predicts surface orientation from images captured under different lighting. The paper describes two complementary sources of information: how one pixel changes across images and how intensities vary spatially within each image. Existing learning approaches tend to emphasize one source while making less use of the other.

GPS-Net combines both forms of processing. For the per-pixel component, an Unstructured Feature Extraction Layer connects an arbitrary number of image-light pairs into graphs. Structure-aware graph convolution then weights the observations to account appropriately for shadows and specular highlights. This graph representation provides a way to process lighting observations without requiring a fixed number of input pairs.

For the spatial component, a Normal Regression Network uses information within images to predict a detailed surface normal map. Experiments on a real-world benchmark report excellent performance with both sparse and dense lighting distributions. The findings support combining variation across lighting conditions with spatial context, so the prediction can draw on evidence about both individual pixels and the surrounding surface.
neurips-2020-gps-net-graph-based-photome.tldr: GPS-Net combines graph-based processing of lighting observations with spatial image features to predict detailed surface normals.

paragraphs: Training graph neural networks can require many labeled nodes, and obtaining those labels can be expensive. Active learning addresses this cost by choosing which nodes to label. This paper studies how to learn that selection strategy so it can be reused on new graphs rather than devised separately for each graph.

The authors formulate node selection as a sequence of decisions on a graph. A graph neural network serves as the policy, and reinforcement learning trains it to choose label queries. Training jointly on several fully labeled source graphs provides experience from which the policy can learn a transferable query strategy.

The learned policy is then applied directly to unlabeled target graphs. Experiments across multiple datasets show improvements in active learning both when transferring within a domain and when transferring across domains. The result supports transferring knowledge about which labels to request, alongside the usual goal of transferring predictive representations. Full labels on the source graphs are part of the training setup; the intended savings concern annotation choices on the target graphs.
neurips-2020-graph-policy-network-for-tr.tldr: A graph-based reinforcement learning policy learns node-label query strategies on source graphs and transfers them to unlabeled target graphs.

paragraphs: Knowledge graphs describe relationships through triplets connecting entities and relations. Many embedding models focus on interactions inside an individual triplet, but useful information can also extend across several connected triplets. Interstellar studies relational paths, where a sequence of triplets supplies both nearby context and longer-range information.

The paper formulates learning along these paths as a recurrent neural architecture search problem. It first analyzes the difficulty of using one unified model as the path-processing architecture. It then proposes searching for recurrent architectures suited to different knowledge graph tasks, making the architecture itself part of the solution rather than fixing the same design across tasks.

A synthetic case study illustrates why the search problem matters. Experiments on real datasets support the effectiveness of the resulting models and the efficiency of the proposed hybrid search algorithm. The contribution combines a modeling perspective with a search method: relationships across multiple triplets deserve explicit treatment, and the recurrent structure used to capture them can be selected for the task at hand.
neurips-2020-interstellar-searching-recu.tldr: Interstellar searches for task-specific recurrent architectures that capture short- and long-range information along knowledge graph paths.

paragraphs: Communication can help multiple learning agents coordinate, but receiving a message does not automatically make it useful. An agent must decide which information matters for its current decision and how that information relates to earlier experience. This paper addresses that selection and reasoning problem with an explicit communication architecture.

The method builds on relational reinforcement learning, using attention to learn relationships among entities. Its memory-based attention network first evaluates the relevance of messages from other agents. It then uses the newly received information to retrieve task-relevant information from memory. Communication and memory therefore work together, allowing current messages to guide how past information is used.

Experiments on cooperative and competitive tasks report substantial improvements over baselines from communication and reasoning over prior information. The authors also demonstrate varied cooperative behaviors across discrete and continuous action spaces, using both on-policy and off-policy gradient methods. These findings support an architecture that learns to interpret messages in context, with empirical breadth across several learning and action settings rather than a claim of universally effective communication.
neurips-2020-learning-multi-agent-commun.tldr: A memory-based attention architecture helps agents select relevant messages and connect them with past information, improving tested multi-agent behaviors.

paragraphs: Directional sensors observe only a limited angle and distance, so their orientations must be coordinated to cover moving targets. Random target movement makes this difficult: sensors can miss targets or redundantly cover the same ones. The paper seeks effective coverage while motivating the need to avoid unnecessary power consumption.

HiT-MAC divides the problem into two levels. A coordinator periodically observes the overall environment and assigns targets to individual executors. Each executor then focuses on tracking its assigned targets. This separation gives the coordinator responsibility for allocation while simplifying the local tracking decisions that executors must learn.

The reinforcement learning framework includes self-attention, an approximation of marginal contributions for the coordinator, and an observation filter conditioned on the executor’s goal. Experiments report advantages over baselines in coverage rate, learning efficiency, and scalability, with ablations examining the introduced components. The stated results support the hierarchical division of coordination and tracking; although low power consumption motivates the problem, the abstract’s reported comparative findings specifically concern coverage, learning, and scaling.
neurips-2020-learning-multi-agent-coordi.tldr: HiT-MAC separates global target assignment from local sensor tracking, improving coverage, learning efficiency, and scalability in experiments.

paragraphs: Neural implicit representations describe shapes through learned functions, offering potential memory benefits at high spatial resolution. To generalize across shapes, a model must learn prior knowledge about the space of those functions. Such knowledge enables reconstruction from observations that may be incomplete or noisy.

Existing approaches represent each shape using a low-dimensional latent code, obtained either through an encoder or through optimization in an auto-decoder framework. MetaSDF instead formulates learning the shape space as a meta-learning problem and applies gradient-based meta-learning. The central change is how shared knowledge across shapes is learned and used for adaptation.

The authors report performance comparable to auto-decoder approaches while making test-time inference an order of magnitude faster. They also report better performance than encoder-decoder methods using pooling-based set encoders. These comparisons show that the proposed formulation can combine effective shape reconstruction with faster inference in the evaluated setting. The result makes learning across a space of shape functions a practical alternative to the latent-code approaches considered in the paper.
neurips-2020-metasdf-meta-learning-signe.tldr: MetaSDF uses gradient-based meta-learning for shape representations, matching auto-decoder performance with roughly tenfold faster test-time inference.

paragraphs: Meta-reinforcement learning trains an agent across tasks so it can adapt efficiently to new ones. That ability can weaken when testing tasks differ from the training distribution. AdMRL addresses this problem by targeting the worst adaptation shortfall within a family of tasks: the gap between optimal return and the return achieved after adaptation.

The method uses a minimax objective and alternates between two operations. It learns a dynamics model on a fixed task, then searches for an adversarial task on which the policy induced by the current model is most suboptimal. This directs training toward weaknesses measured relative to what could be achieved on each task.

Assuming the task family has a parameterized representation, the authors derive gradients through the implicit function theorem and implement their estimator using conjugate gradients and REINFORCE. Continuous control experiments support improvements in worst-case performance, generalization to out-of-distribution tasks, and training and testing sample efficiency over existing methods. These are empirical findings; minimizing worst-case suboptimality is the training objective, not an unconditional guarantee of optimal adaptation.
neurips-2020-model-based-adversarial-met.tldr: AdMRL trains against tasks where adaptation is most suboptimal, improving robustness and sample efficiency in continuous control experiments.

paragraphs: When linear regression has more coefficients than training examples, the choice of regularization can strongly affect prediction. This paper studies weighted ridge regression, where a matrix determines how different coefficient directions are regularized. It allows general data covariance and a prior in which the true coefficients have different amounts of variation in different directions.

Under a random design model, the authors exactly characterize prediction risk in a proportional asymptotic limit: both dimensions grow while their ratio approaches a fixed value greater than one. Within this setting, they give conditions determining whether the optimal ridge parameter is positive or negative. The possibility of a negative optimum supports an interpretation in which overparameterization already supplies an implicit regularization effect.

The analysis also characterizes double descent for principal component regression with non-isotropic data and coefficients. Finally, it determines optimal weighting matrices for both the ridgeless limit and optimally regularized regression, and demonstrates advantages over standard ridge and principal component regression. These conclusions describe the paper’s specified statistical and asymptotic setting, including its directional structure.
neurips-2020-on-the-optimal-weighted-ell.tldr: An asymptotic analysis identifies optimal weighted ridge regularization and conditions allowing a negative optimal ridge parameter in overparameterized regression.

paragraphs: Identity testing asks whether samples fit a specified probability distribution. This paper studies how to perform that test with differential privacy for high-dimensional distribution families. Its targets include multivariate Gaussians with known covariance and product distributions whose coordinates take values of either minus one or plus one.

The proposed testers improve the number of samples needed compared with approaches derived from earlier techniques. In many parameter regimes, their sample complexity matches the order-optimal minimax rate O(d^1/2/alpha²). This qualification matters: the matching result applies across many regimes, rather than being asserted for every possible parameter choice.

The authors construct two types of testers with different tradeoffs between sample requirements and computation. They also establish a two-way reduction connecting a subclass of multivariate product distributions to univariate distribution testing, which yields upper and lower bounds for that subclass. Together, the results clarify both what private testing can achieve with limited data and how computational choices affect that goal for the studied families.
neurips-2020-private-identity-testing-fo.tldr: New private goodness-of-fit testers achieve improved sample complexity, matching an order-optimal rate in many parameter regimes.

paragraphs: The numerical formats used during inference affect the cost of serving deep learning models. This paper studies Microsoft Floating Point, a family of datatypes developed for production cloud inference on custom hardware. The approach develops numerical algorithms and hardware together, making the representation of numbers part of the system design.

The authors report threefold lower cost for MSFP16 relative to Bfloat16 and fourfold lower cost for MSFP12 relative to INT8, with comparable or better accuracy. They also report an accuracy impact below one percent and no required changes to model topology. These claims concern the MSFP implementations and production settings studied in the paper.

MSFP supports convolutional networks, recurrent networks, and Transformers without modification and is integrated into an established cloud production pipeline. Evaluations include models used for web search, question answering, and image classification. The contribution is therefore both a numerical format and evidence of its deployment practicality: substantial reported cost reductions can coexist with small accuracy effects across several model classes and production applications.
neurips-2020-pushing-the-limits-of-narro.tldr: MSFP combines custom hardware and narrow-precision datatypes to reduce reported inference costs while preserving accuracy across production model classes.

paragraphs: Heterogeneous graphs contain multiple kinds of nodes and edges, so their connections carry varied semantic information. Auxiliary learning tasks can improve graph representations, but selecting useful tasks for this richer structure is a challenge. This paper builds such tasks from meta-paths, which describe composite relationships formed by sequences of different edge types.

The method trains a graph neural network on a primary task while using meta-path prediction as self-supervised auxiliary work. It learns which combination of auxiliary tasks is effective and how to balance their contributions. The authors frame this as a form of meta-learning because the auxiliary learning process itself is adjusted to help the primary objective.

The approach is designed as a plug-in for graph neural networks and requires neither manual labeling for the auxiliary tasks nor additional data. Experiments show consistent improvements in link prediction and node classification on heterogeneous graphs. The findings support using existing graph structure as extra supervision while learning how much each structural prediction task should contribute to the main task.
neurips-2020-self-supervised-auxiliary-l.tldr: Self-supervised meta-path prediction supplies automatically balanced auxiliary tasks that improve heterogeneous graph learning in experiments.

paragraphs: Clustering becomes difficult when each example has many features, especially when only a few distinguish the underlying groups. Sparse clustering aims to focus on those relevant features. The paper identifies two practical obstacles in existing approaches: computationally expensive outer procedures around k-means and shrinkage parameters that require careful tuning.

The proposed framework uses feature ranking for sparse k-means clustering. The authors describe it as intuitive, simple to implement, and competitive with state-of-the-art methods. They also establish consistency and convergence guarantees, giving theoretical support to the algorithm alongside its practical simplicity.

The core approach extends to tasks involving subsets of attributes and partially observed data. Evaluation includes simulated experiments, real datasets, and a study of protein expression in trisomic mice. These results support the framework’s usefulness across the tested settings. Its motivation is especially relevant when many measured features contribute little to separating clusters, so selecting features is part of discovering meaningful groups rather than merely an optional preprocessing step.
neurips-2020-simple-and-scalable-sparse-.tldr: A feature-ranking framework makes sparse k-means simple and scalable, with theoretical guarantees and competitive empirical results.

paragraphs: Large parallel training systems can compute gradients faster than their data pipelines can deliver fresh batches. In that situation, preprocessing and storage, memory, or network operations become the bottleneck. Data echoing uses the waiting time to take additional gradient steps on the batch already available.

This paper provides convergence analyses for data-echoed versions of common optimization methods. The analysis asks whether reusing a batch can offer a provable advantage over synchronous methods that wait for fresh data. Its stated setting is convex optimization with stochastic minibatches, which defines the scope of the theoretical conclusions.

The authors show improvements in the curvature-dominated part of the convergence rate while retaining the optimal statistical rate. The distinction matters: repeated computation on existing data can accelerate one component of optimization without being treated as additional independent information. These results give theoretical support to echoing when data delivery lags behind computation and explain which part of convergence benefits from the extra work performed on a batch.
neurips-2020-stochastic-optimization-wit.tldr: For convex stochastic optimization, data echoing improves curvature-related convergence while preserving the optimal statistical rate.

paragraphs: GAN training involves a minimax objective with a difficult global shape, creating opportunities for optimization to reach poor solutions. This paper studies the empirical loss landscape to understand how the choice of objective contributes to that difficulty. It focuses on whether the landscape contains bad basins associated with mode collapse.

The authors prove that a class of separable GAN objectives, including the original JS-GAN, contains exponentially many such basins. They then analyze relativistic pairing GAN loss, which couples generated samples with real samples, and prove that it has no bad basins in their landscape analysis. This identifies a consequential structural difference between the objectives.

Synthetic experiments show that a predicted bad basin can occur during training. Further experiments support the proposed landscape advantage, including better performance for the pairing objective with relatively narrow neural networks. The theoretical and empirical findings together motivate changing the loss to improve training geometry. The absence of bad basins is the specific proved property, rather than a blanket claim that every aspect of GAN optimization is solved.
neurips-2020-towards-a-better-global-los.tldr: The paper proves a bad-basin advantage for relativistic pairing GAN loss over a class of separable objectives and supports it experimentally.

paragraphs: Deep steganography can hide an entire image inside another image, but understanding how the secret is encoded is difficult when encoding depends on the cover. Universal Deep Hiding separates these operations by encoding the secret independently of the cover image. This makes the encoded message available for analysis on its own.

Using that separation, the authors attribute the success of deep image hiding to a frequency discrepancy between the cover and the encoded secret. They also report performance comparable to existing cover-dependent methods. The result suggests that cover-independent encoding can preserve effectiveness while making the hiding mechanism easier to examine.

The paper extends the architecture to universal watermarking and light field messaging. It reports robustness to a pixel intensity shift in the container image, a property relevant to the latter application. The authors also claim the first demonstration of full-image hiding with deep neural networks for watermarking and light field messaging. These findings connect the architecture’s independent encoding to both analysis and applications beyond hiding a single image in a conventional cover.
neurips-2020-udh-universal-deep-hiding-f.tldr: UDH encodes secret images independently of covers, enabling analysis and extending comparable image-hiding performance to watermarking and light field messaging.

paragraphs: QMIX supports centralized training and decentralized decisions by combining individual agents’ utilities monotonically. This makes decentralization convenient but limits the joint values it can represent. In particular, it cannot capture every situation where one agent’s preference among actions changes depending on what other agents do.

The paper analyzes QMIX as a projection of learning targets into its representable value functions. Its ordinary squared-error projection weights every joint action equally and can miss the optimal policy even when given the true optimal values. Weighted QMIX instead emphasizes better joint actions. The authors propose two weighting schemes and prove that their projections recover the correct maximizing action for any joint action values.

Building on the tabular analysis, the paper introduces scalable Centrally-Weighted and Optimistically-Weighted variants. Both show improved performance on predator-prey and challenging multi-agent StarCraft tasks. The distinction between results matters: correct action recovery is proved for the analyzed weighting schemes, while the scalable algorithms are supported by experiments. The approach targets which decisions survive approximation, rather than requiring exact representation of every joint value.
neurips-2020-weighted-qmix-expanding-mon.tldr: Weighted QMIX emphasizes better joint actions during value approximation, with action-recovery guarantees in its analysis and improved benchmark performance.
